WELCOME TO
CLOUD COMPUTING
VIRTUALIZATION
PART 09
Part 9: Virtualization
✓ Define and explain virtualization in detail.
✓ Discuss the history of virtualization development.
✓ Presents the different types of virtualization in detail.
✓ List the pros and cons of virtualization.
✓ Identify applications that are suitable, as well as those
that are not, for virtualization.
✓ Analyze why companies should use virtualization.
❖ Objectives
Part 9: Virtualization
✓ Virtualization is the process of creating a virtual
version of something, such as an operating system,
server, storage device, or network
❖ Definition
Part 9: Virtualization
✓ Increase resource usage efficiency: Helps make
maximum use of hardware capabilities.
✓ Cost savings: Reduced need for physical hardware.
✓ Flexible and scalable: Easily expand or contract
resources as needed.
❖ Benefits of Virtualization
Part 9: Virtualization
✓ Server Virtualization: Create multiple virtual
machines from one physical server.
✓ Desktop Virtualization: Run multiple operating
systems on one desktop.
✓ Storage Virtualization: Combine multiple storage
devices into a single storage unit.
❖ Types of Virtualization
Part 9: Virtualization
✓ Virtual memory is a memory management technology
that allows computers to compensate for physical
RAM shortages by using space on the hard disk.
❖ Introduction to Virtual Memory
➢ Definition
Part 9: Virtualization
✓ Virtual memory combines physical RAM with storage
space on the hard drive.
✓ When physical RAM is full, the operating system
moves less used memory pages from RAM to virtual
memory.
❖ Introduction to Virtual Memory
➢ Principle of Operation
Part 9: Virtualization
✓ Increase available memory capacity: Allows running
applications that require more memory than the
amount of physical RAM available.
✓ Improve system performance: Minimize memory
shortages and improve overall performance.
✓ Optimized memory management: The operating
system can manage memory more effectively.
❖ Introduction to Virtual Memory
➢ Benefits of Virtual Memory
Part 9: Virtualization
✓ Physical RAM: Random access memory provides fast
access speeds for running tasks.
✓ Space on hard disk: The storage space is used by the
operating system as extended memory.
❖ Introduction to Virtual Memory
➢ Components of Virtual Memory
Part 9: Virtualization
✓ Memory Pages: Data is divided into small blocks
called pages.
✓ Swapping: The process of switching memory pages
between RAM and hard disk space as needed.
❖ Introduction to Virtual Memory
➢ How It Works
Part 9: Virtualization
✓ Cost effective: Using hard disks as virtual memory
reduces costs compared to upgrading physical RAM.
✓ Flexible: Easily adjust the size of virtual memory
according to needs.
✓ Ability of extension: Increase system processing
capacity without changing hardware.
❖ Introduction to Virtual Memory
➢ Advantages of Virtual Memory
Part 9: Virtualization
✓ Access speed is slower than RAM: Accessing virtual
memory is slower than accessing physical RAM due
to the speed limit of the hard disk.
✓ Consumes hard disk resources: Using hard disk space
as virtual memory can affect overall storage capacity.
❖ Introduction to Virtual Memory
➢ Disadvantages of Virtual Memory
Part 9: Virtualization
✓ Green computing is the effective use of
information and communications technologies
(ICT) to reduce negative impacts on the
environment and save energy
❖ Green Computing
➢ Definition
Part 9: Virtualization
✓ Energy saving: Reduce energy consumption of
IT devices.
✓ Reduce carbon emissions: Limit carbon
dioxide (CO2) emissions from IT operations.
✓ Reuse and recycle: Encourage reuse and
recycling of IT equipment to reduce e-waste.
❖ Green Computing
➢ Goal of Green Computing
Part 9: Virtualization
✓ Power off the device when not in use: Reduce
energy consumption by turning off computers,
printers and other devices when not in use.
✓ Use power management features: Take advantage
of operating system and hardware power
management features to save power.
❖ Green Computing
➢ Green Computing Solutions
Part 9: Virtualization
✓ Minimize unnecessary printing: Use electronic
documents instead of paper printing to reduce paper
consumption.
✓ Use energy-saving equipment: Choose appliances
❖ Green Computing
➢ Green Computing Solutions
Part 9: Virtualization
✓ Server virtualization is a technology that
allows creating multiple virtual servers from a
single physical server, helping to optimize
resources and improve efficiency.
❖ Introduction to Server Virtualization
➢ Definition
Part 9: Virtualization
✓ Hyper-V is a virtualization technology from
Microsoft, built into Windows Server versions.
✓ Allows creation and management of virtual
machines (VMs) on a physical server.
❖ Introduction to Server Virtualization
➢ Microsoft Hyper-V
Part 9: Virtualization
✓ Server consolidation: Reduce the number of physical
servers needed by running multiple virtual machines on
a single server.
✓ Increase CPU usage efficiency: Optimize CPU
resources by distributing load among virtual machines.
✓ Improved load balancing: Distributes workload evenly
among virtual machines to ensure optimal performance.
❖ Introduction to Server Virtualization
➢ Microsoft Hyper-V - Benefits
Part 9: Virtualization
✓ Create and manage virtual machines: Easily create,
configure, and manage virtual machines.
✓ Supports many operating systems: Run many different
operating systems on the same physical server.
✓ Integration with Windows Server: Built-in to Windows
Server, no need to install additional software.
❖ Introduction to Server Virtualization
➢ Microsoft Hyper-V - Features of Hyper-V
Part 9: Virtualization
✓ Create and manage virtual machines: Easily create,
configure, and manage virtual machines.
✓ Supports many operating systems: Run many different
operating systems on the same physical server.
✓ Integration with Windows Server: Built-in to Windows
Server, no need to install additional software.
❖ Introduction to Server Virtualization
➢ Microsoft Hyper-V - Benefit of economic
Part 9: Virtualization
✓ Deploying IT infrastructure
✓ Software development and testing
✓ Backup and disaster recovery solutions
❖ Introduction to Server Virtualization
➢ Features of Hyper-V –
▪ Practical applications of Hyper-V
Part 9: Virtualization
✓ Define:
✓ VMware ESXi is an enterprise-grade virtualization
platform developed by VMware, providing a powerful
and efficient virtualization solution for servers.
✓ Outstanding features:
✓ ESXi is a type 1 hypervisor, meaning it runs directly
on the server hardware without the need for an
underlying operating system.
❖ Introduction to VMware ESXi
Part 9: Virtualization
✓ High performance: Provides high virtualization
performance thanks to hardware and software optimization.
✓ Centralized management: Easily manage multiple virtual
machines and system resources through vCenter Server.
✓ Security and stability: Integrates advanced security features
and is highly reliable.
❖ Introduction to VMware ESXi
➢ Benefits of VMware ESXi
Part 9: Virtualization
✓ VMware vSphere Hypervisor: Create and manage high-
performance virtual machines.
✓ vMotion: Move virtual machines between physical servers
without disrupting service.
✓ Distributed Resource Scheduler (DRS): Automatically
distribute resources to optimize system performance.
❖ Introduction to VMware ESXi
➢ Key Features of VMware ESXi
Part 9: Virtualization
✓ Centralized management: vCenter Server allows
centralized management of virtual machines and
virtualized resources.
✓ Main feature: Manage resources, deploy virtual
machines, and monitor system performance.
❖ Introduction to VMware ESXi
➢ VMware vCenter Server
Part 9: Virtualization
✓ Centralized management: vCenter Server allows
centralized management of virtual machines and
virtualized resources.
✓ Main feature: Manage resources, deploy virtual machines,
and monitor system performance.
❖ Introduction to VMware ESXi
➢ VMware vCenter Server
Part 9: Virtualization
✓ Implementation process: Install ESXi directly onto the
server hardware. Configure basic parameters and connect
to vCenter Server.
✓ Use: Create and manage virtual machines, monitor
performance, and optimize resources through the vSphere
Client management interface.
❖ Introduction to VMware ESXi
➢ Deploying and Using VMware ESXi
Part 9: Virtualization
✓ Parallels Desktop: Leading desktop virtualization software.
✓ Main function: Supports multiple operating systems
(Windows and Linux). Easily switch between operating
systems.
❖ Introduction to Parallels Desktop
Part 9: Virtualization
✓ Save hardware costs: Reduce the need to buy additional
hardware.
✓ Energy saving: Consumes less energy than using multiple
physical computers.
✓ Increase work efficiency: Allows flexible switching
between different working environments.
❖ Introduction to Parallels Desktop
➢ Advantages of Parallels Desktop
Part 9: Virtualization
✓ Software programming and testing: Programmers can test
code on many operating systems.
✓ Customer support: Support staff can quickly switch
between operating systems to resolve customer issues.
✓ Training and development: The training environment uses
many different operating systems on the same computer.
❖ Introduction to Parallels Desktop
➢ Applications of Parallels Desktop in Business
Part 9: Virtualization
✓ Resource consumption: Requires higher system resources
to run virtualization.
✓ Performance: Performance may not be as good as when
running on a standalone physical system.
✓ Complex management: Requires complex management
and configuration for maximum efficiency.
❖ Introduction to Parallels Desktop
➢ Disadvantages of Parallels Desktop
Part 9: Virtualization
✓ Microsoft Desktop Virtualization: Desktop
virtualization solution.
✓ Main tools: Microsoft VDI (Virtual Desktop
Infrastructure) Microsoft App-V (Application
Virtualization)
❖ Introduction to Microsoft Desktop Virtualization
Part 9: Virtualization
✓ Microsoft VDI: Virtualized desktop infrastructure.
✓ Main function: Provides virtualized operating
system and application environments. Enhanced
security and centralized management.
❖ Introduction to Microsoft Desktop Virtualization
➢ Microsoft VDI (Virtual Desktop Infrastructure)
Part 9: Virtualization
✓ Microsoft VDI: Virtualized desktop infrastructure.
✓ Main function: Provides virtualized operating
system and application environments. Enhanced
security and centralized management.
❖ Introduction to Microsoft Desktop Virtualization
➢ Microsoft VDI (Virtual Desktop Infrastructure)
Part 9: Virtualization
✓ Microsoft App-V: Application virtualization.
✓ Main function:
✓ Deploy applications quickly.
✓ Reduce software conflicts and increase
application portability.
❖ Introduction to Microsoft Desktop Virtualization
➢ Microsoft App-V (Application Virtualization)
Part 9: Virtualization
✓ Simplify management:
✓ Manage desktops and applications from one centralized
interface.
✓ Flexible access:
✓ Access user profiles and data from any computer.
✓ Enhanced security:
✓ Improve software license management and data security.
❖ Introduction to Microsoft Desktop Virtualization
➢ Advantages of Microsoft Desktop Virtualization
Part 9: Virtualization
✓ Enterprise: Deployed in the corporate working
environment.
✓ Education: Use in school computer rooms.
✓ Government: Virtualization in government agencies
to protect sensitive data.
❖ Introduction to Microsoft Desktop Virtualization
➢ Practical Applications of Microsoft Desktop Virtualization
Part 9: Virtualization
✓ VMware View: Solution for providing virtual
desktops on demand.
✓ Main function:
✓ Provides centralized operating systems and
applications.
✓ Enhance security and effective management.
❖ Introduction to VMware View
Part 9: Virtualization
✓ Simplify management: Manage operating systems
and applications from one central interface.
✓ Automatic provisioning: Create accounts and
automatic desktop backups.
✓ Manage virtual desktop files: Manage and store files
on virtual desktops easily.
❖ Introduction to VMware View
➢ VMware View Features
Part 9: Virtualization
✓ Supports multiple platforms: Compatible with
Windows, macOS, Linux and other operating
systems.
✓ Ability of extension: Easily expandable to meet
business growth needs.
❖ Introduction to VMware View
➢ Supports Diverse Platforms
Part 9: Virtualization
✓ Enhanced security: Data and applications are stored
on a central server.
✓ Flexible access: Users can access the work
environment from any device.
✓ Reduce management costs: Simplify system
deployment and maintenance.
❖ Introduction to VMware View
➢ Advantages of VMware View
Part 9: Virtualization
✓ VPN (Virtual Private Network): Virtual private
network helps connect securely over the Internet.
✓ Applications of VPN on Windows:
✓ Create secure connections for remote
employees.
✓ Access the company's intranet remotely.
❖ Introduction to VPN on Windows
Part 9: Virtualization
✓ Security: Encrypt connection to protect data.
✓ Flexibility: Supports many VPN protocols (PPTP,
L2TP/IPsec, SSTP, IKEv2).
✓ Compatibility: Built-in to Windows, easy to install
and use.
❖ Introduction to VPN on Windows
➢ Features of VPN on Windows
Part 9: Virtualization
✓ Easy to use: Provides a user-friendly interface and is
easy to set up.
✓ High security: Uses advanced security protocols.
✓ Economics: No need to invest in third-party
software.
❖ Introduction to VPN on Windows
➢ Advantages of VPN on Windows
Part 9: Virtualization
✓ Enterprise:
✓ Secure connection for remote workers.
✓ Education:
✓ Support students and teachers to access remote
learning materials.
✓ Government:
✓ Secure access to important information systems.
❖ Introduction to VPN on Windows
➢ Practical Applications of VPN on Windows
